title: Electric charge, field and potential
note: Charge comes in two signs, is conserved, and is quantized in units of e. Coulomb's law gives the force between point charges; the electric field E = F/q describes that force per unit charge at each point. Electric potential V is potential energy per unit charge, and fields point from high to low potential.

read.title: Fields and potentials
text: Ordinary matter is full of charge: positive protons in nuclei and negative electrons around them. Usually the two balance. Rubbing a balloon on hair moves some electrons from one to the other, leaving both charged but conserving the total. Charge always comes in whole multiples of e, 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

Coulomb's law gives the force between two point charges: proportional to the product of the charges and to 1/r², just like gravity, but far stronger and able to repel as well as attract. Rather than thinking of charges acting across empty space, physicists describe an electric field filling the space around a charge. A test charge q placed anywhere feels a force qE. Field lines start on positive charges and end on negative ones.

Potential is the energy view of the same idea. The electric potential at a point is the potential energy per unit charge there, measured in volts, where one volt is one joule per coulomb. A positive charge released in a field accelerates toward lower potential, gaining kinetic energy, much as a ball rolls downhill. Surfaces of constant potential always cross field lines at right angles, so moving a charge along one takes no work.
